justification_quote: Abstract: "effectively validated on various supervised, unsupervised, and reinforcement learning tasks"; instances: DVS-CIFAR10/DVS-Gesture (Table I), MNIST/Fashion-MNIST 97.9%/87.0% (Sec III-A-2), Flappy Bird and UAV decision making (Sec III-B), melody memory 99% (Sec III-D), Emotion6 (Sec III-E).

justification_quote: Abstract: "These brain-inspired AI models have been effectively validated on various supervised, unsupervised, and reinforcement learning tasks, and they can be used to enable AI models to be with multiple brain-inspired cognitive functions"; Secs III-IV enumerate those validations (Table I, Fig 9, Fig 15, Fig 20).

justification_quote: Sec I: "Physiological studies in recent years have established a causal relationship between heterogeneous dendritic axons and the firing properties of neurons [8], neuronal heterogeneity plays an important role in determining the function of neural circuits [9]-[11] and determines the frequency of the neural spike signal [12]" — attributions carried entirely by citation; no biological evidence presented in the paper.

justification_quote: Sec I: TaiBai "designed from the ground up to encapsulate essential biological principles of neuronal heterogeneity, synaptic heterogeneity, flexible network topologies, and on-chip synaptic plasticity"; the mapping is instantiated by deploying diverse models on-chip (dendritic DHSNN with 4 branches, heterogeneous-neuron SRNN, on-chip learning BCI; Sec V-B-3, Fig 15), one demonstration setting per mechanism.
note: Mapping from brain principles to chip components (CC cores ~ cortical columns, event-driven scheduler ~ event-driven sparse computation) is stated, but no measurement of mapping fidelity itself.

justification_quote: Sec V-C-4: "Fig. 15 includes a TaiBai-homogeneous baseline, obtained by deploying SRNN without heterogeneous neurons, DHSFNN without dendrites, and BCI cross-day decoding without on-chip learning. As can be seen from the figure, the heterogeneous neuron model makes it easier to identify the band type of ECG data, the DHSFNN with a dendritic model significantly improves the network performance, and the on-chip learning capability improves the decoding accuracy across days"; plus GPU benchmark at comparable accuracy (Fig 13(d), Fig 15).
note: On-chip ablation (same platform, biologically-inspired component removed) isolates correspondence from platform; GPU comparison gives the efficiency claim. Residual confound: simulator-based power estimates vs measured GPU.

justification_quote: Three task families demonstrated (ECG QTDB, speech SHD, cross-day macaque BCI; Sec V-B-3) plus standard SNN benchmarks (Fig 13(d)); scale trade-off reported once: "the number of cores increases by 4 times (182 to 749), and energy efficiency decreases by 1.7 times (6190 to 3590)" (Fig 13(e)).
note: Multiple families demonstrated, but each bio-mechanism gain (heterogeneity, dendrites, on-chip learning) is shown in its own task only; no cross-family or cross-scale ablation of a single gain.

justification_quote: Abstract: "These results demonstrated its high potentiation as a scalable, programmable, and ultra-efficient solution for both multi-scale brain simulation and brain-inspired computation" — but the evaluation covers only AI tasks (ECG, speech, BCI, SNN benchmarks); no brain-simulation experiment is presented anywhere in the paper (grep: simulation appears only in motivation and references).
note: The efficiency half of the abstract claim is linked to results (Fig 15: power efficiency 296-855x GPU at comparable accuracy); the multi-scale brain-simulation half is asserted from design capability without a demonstrated simulation.

justification_quote: Sec II: region-function attributions carried entirely by citation, e.g., "the prefrontal cortex (PFC), as its core module, is responsible for decision-making, regulating planning, execution, and task management [47]"; Brodmann [45] and HCP [46] frameworks described from literature; no biological evidence presented in the paper.
note: Attributions are standard neuroscience labels cited from reviews and parcellation papers; no specific source independently verified by me, so external stays E0.

justification_quote: Sec I/III-A propose a mapping only: "the V1 cortical area ... is responsible for primary extraction of complex visual features, which can be implemented using CNN or YOLO [39]; ... the FPC region in the prefrontal cortex ... which we seek to emulate using LLMs"; "we simplified the corresponding functional connectivity networks, restricting interactions solely to the existing functional nodes" — no system is built or run anywhere in the paper.
note: Correspondence is asserted as a design concept (Table I mapping brain areas to modules); zero instantiation evidence because nothing is implemented.

justification_quote: Abstract: "Implementing these structures within an agent enables it to achieve basic cognitive intelligence akin to human capabilities" — the paper contains no experiment, no implementation, and no comparison; the only feasibility argument is a literature survey (Table II: "currently implemented agent architectures share similar brain-inspired structural ideas").
note: Utility is claimed prospectively; validation is named as a future goal ("The goal is to construct a brain-inspired agent architecture and validate whether this structure can perform well on general cognitive tasks").

justification_quote: No demonstrated setting exists, so generality cannot be assessed; the limitations section lists open challenges ("significant limitations and challenges remain before realizing a brain-inspired agent capable of human-level intelligence") without any tested or untested task families.
note: Concept paper: no task families, scales or ablations exist to evaluate.

justification_quote: Abstract claims a capability outcome ("enables it to achieve basic cognitive intelligence akin to human capabilities") while the paper presents an unimplemented proposal; Chapter IV concedes "significant limitations and challenges remain before realizing a brain-inspired agent capable of human-level intelligence" — the evidence scope is an argument by analogy plus a survey, not a demonstration.
note: Claim scope (achieved cognitive capability) exceeds evidence scope (concept and literature plausibility); the enabling verb is not hedged in the abstract.

justification_quote: Abstract/Sec 1: "humans have a strong generalisation ability which is beneficial from the structural and functional asymmetry of the two sides of the brain"; supported only by "converging evidence from structural and functional neuroimaging studies ... [12]" and an evolution review [13] — citation only, no biological evidence in the paper, and the asymmetry-causes-generalisation attribution itself is not evidenced.
note: Cited neuroimaging works ([12],[13]) not independently verified by me; external stays E0.

justification_quote: Sec 1/3.2: "the design of dual NCP architectures replicates the human brain left and right hemispheres", with asymmetric wirings per side (Fig 3c: Left NCP 3/5 vs Right NCP 4/6); NCP itself is "inspired by C. elegans organism nervous system [16]". No evidence beyond naming that two sparse RNNs instantiate hemispheric computation; "Any instance of the LTC is essentially an RNN".
note: Correspondence is a design analogy; nothing tests whether the dual-NCP computation matches the biological asymmetry mechanism.

justification_quote: Sec 4.3: "the brain-inspired (CNN-DNCP v2) model can reduce 6.57% error when comparing with CNN model on Udacity dataset" (Fig 5.a); "The brain-inspired architecture (CNN-DNCP v4) is 5.80% and 34.05% more effective than the CNN model with regard to MSE on the cloudy and night time comma.ai recordings". The architecture grid includes single-NCP vs dual-NCP variants sharing the same CNN head (Fig 3, Sec 3.2), partially isolating the duality design; training MSE honestly reported as favouring CNN.
note: Controlled comparisons exist for the generalisation claim; CNN-vs-NCP contrast is architecture-confounded, but single-vs-dual NCP variants and the fixed CNN head narrow the attribution.

justification_quote: Generalisation tested across domains within one task family: trained on Udacity lakeside, tested on jungle; trained on comma.ai sunny, tested on cloudy/night (Sec 4.1/4.3, Fig 5) — the demonstrated gain survives several domain shifts but no other task family, scale or systematic ablation is evaluated.
note: Multiple unseen-domain settings, single task (steering MSE); no scale or cross-family evidence.

justification_quote: Abstract: "our brain-inspired method outperforms existing methods regarding generalisation when dealing with unseen data" — evidence compares against the single reference CNN [2] plus the authors' own variants (Sec 1: "put into competition with the reference neural network mentioned in [2]"), and one variant was dropped for poor training results (Sec 4.1: "the CNN-DNCP model architecture is dropped since it takes way too long to train and the loss result is strikingly unsatisfactory").
note: "Existing methods" (plural, generic) is broader than the one reference architecture actually compared; generalisation direction of the claim is supported, its comparative breadth is not.

justification_quote: Sec 1: brain attributions carried by citation only and acknowledged as loose: "These techniques draw loose inspiration from models of brain computations"; "Traditional NN architectures lack the concept of locality, whereas brain-inspired NN architectures prioritize it, leading to modularity ... Moreover, brain-inspired NNs tend to exhibit high sparsity" ([4],[13],[15],[16]); no biological evidence is presented.
note: The structure-function attribution (brain organization is local/sparse/modular) rests on citations to brain-inspired ML papers, not on neuroscience evidence inspected here.

justification_quote: Sec 2/3.1: stated mapping from brain principles to mechanisms: locality -> per-unit coordinates with L1 distance penalty ("A hyperparameter A, related to the network size, regulates the importance of locality"), sparsity -> Lasso penalization, modularity -> composed modules; demonstrated instantiation: the trained PINN "evolve[s] from a fully connected MLP PINN to a sparse and modular" architecture (Fig 2).
note: The mapping is operational and the structural outcome is demonstrated, but the correspondence to biology is by the paper's own wording loose; no measurement of biological fidelity.

justification_quote: Sec 4: same-problem controlled comparisons: "The final error for the brain-inspired and fully-connected PINNs are 0.023 and 0.0094, respectively ... the brain-inspired PINN has approximately twice the error of the fully connected MLP PINN" (resource-accuracy trade-off, disclosed); "the modular PINN has a test error (calculated as MSE) that is approximately two orders lower than the fully-connected MLP PINN" (Fig 5, 3 modules of 3 units vs 9-unit MLP).
note: The utility claim (compact architectures, minimal compute/memory at acceptable accuracy) has its own comparisons; the accuracy cost of sparsification is honestly reported rather than hidden.

justification_quote: All evidence is on 1D Poisson-type equations with harmonic sources ("For demonstration purposes, this work focuses on solving the one-dimensional Poisson equation", Sec 3.1) plus a spectral-bias demonstration that high-frequency problems need more units; no other PDE family, dimensionality or systematic scale sweep is evaluated.
note: Multiple related instances within one toy problem family; generality beyond it is untested.

justification_quote: Abstract: "Our experiments show that brain-inspired PINN training leads to PINN architectures that minimize the computing and memory resources yet provide accurate results" — Sec 4 shows exactly this on 1D Poisson problems with the accuracy loss disclosed ("only affected by a small loss of accuracy when compared to large fully-connected MLP"); the demonstration-only scope is stated in Sec 3.1.
note: Claim phrasing tracks the experiments closely; the 1D-only demonstration scope is openly flagged, keeping abstract and evidence scopes aligned.

LI plays a role in amplifying the perception of various sensory stimuli [56] and MI is linked to the rhythmic activity of neural networks [57], [58]"; no biological evidence presented.

justification_quote: Sec III-B/Fig 2: stated mapping from biology to architecture — "the search space ... includes local modular structure consisting of five neural motifs [FE, FI, FbI, LI, MI], and global free long-term connectivity between modules"; "We implement them with spiking neurons as shown in Fig. 2b"; modules are brain-region-inspired. justification_quote: Sec IV-B: component ablations with the evolutionary process held constant ("Except for the variables mentioned in the ablation experiments, the parameters and process of the evolutionary algorithm are kept constant"): motif-combination ablation ("the classification accuracy of EB-NAS is 0.88%, 1.13%, 1.18% and 2.15% higher than the best single-motif model") and connectivity ablation vs hierarchical CL-0 ("2.35%, 2.54%, 1.58% and 3.17% higher"); plus SOTA SNN comparisons (Tables III-IV) and spike-count energy comparisons.

justification_quote: Gains replicated across four datasets spanning static (CIFAR10, CIFAR100) and neuromorphic (CIFAR10-DVS, DVS128-Gesture) data with ablations repeated on each (Sec IV-B), but every setting is image classification; no other task family and no parameter/scale sweep of the gain is reported.

justification_quote: Abstract: "Extensive experiments on static datasets (CIFAR10, CIFAR100) and neuromorphic datasets (CIFAR10-DVS, DVS128-Gesture) demonstrate that our proposed model boosts energy efficiency, archiving consistent and remarkable performance" — Tables III-IV and the spike-count comparisons support accuracy and energy claims on exactly these datasets; the reverse claim is hedged as "preliminary insights".
note: Abstract enumerates the exact datasets used; no scope beyond demonstrated tasks is claimed.

note: Numbers in the abstract match the tables; the improvement claim (accuracy without extra FLOPs) is what the ablations and Pareto plots show.

justification_quote: Sec 4.2 Table 1: controlled grid over spiking (ST) and modulate-block (M-Block) factors: DPT 0.707/0.860/0.720/0.540 vs STMDP 0.754/0.940/0.800/0.540 on PushT/Can/Square/ToolHang; Table 2 ablation isolates the SMD module.
